children: Indian pharmaceutical ingredients manufacturer Lee Pharma is studying the establishment of a new manufacturing plant in Egypt as part of plans to expand its presence in the country and African markets, local Arabic language news portal Al Borsa reported last week.
Lamia El-Sayed, the company's business development official, told the newspaper that Lee Pharma is evaluating the proposed facility as part of its expansion strategy.
The report did not disclose the planned investment, production capacity, location or development timeline for the plant.

Lee Pharma, which manufactures pharmaceutical raw materials and active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), expects its sales in Egypt to exceed $5 million in 2026, compared with $3 million in 2025, supported by the introduction of new products.

The company currently supplies 100 pharmaceutical raw materials to 55 manufacturers in Egypt, with its products used in medicines for diabetes, pain management, psychiatric and cardiovascular conditions and weight loss, according to the report.
Lee Pharma has operated in Egypt since 2000 and established a regional office in 2023 to manage its Middle East and North Africa operations.
El-Sayed said the company has started discussions with Egyptian pharmaceutical manufacturers on long-term partnerships and supply agreements.
It is also planning to expand into Nigeria, Ghana, Ethiopia and Namibia from 2027, with Egypt viewed as a gateway for its African expansion.
The company is seeking to supply state-owned and private pharmaceutical manufacturers with raw materials used in products tendered through Egypt's Unified Procurement Authority (UPA), she added.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)

title: India’s Lee Pharma studies new pharmaceutical ingredients plant in Egypt
